target_customer: US tech companies, especially startups, that want to hire and manage software engineers in Latin America in US time zones
problem: US startups in Austin could not compete for engineering talent and needed vetted developers, payroll, benefits and equipment handled in Latin America.
business_model: management fee on top of developer salary, benefits and taxes (15 percent fee stated at the YC launch)
product_category: nearshore engineering staffing and employer of record services

founders.name: Jacqueline Samira
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2022-08-29 says she and Licea worked at OwnLocal in Austin; the Launch HN post says she worked in sales there.

founders.name: Frank Licea
founders.background_notes: Launch HN post says he was a software developer and product manager at Austin startups and large companies and speaks Spanish; listed as Founder on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A service business with a recruiting and matching algorithm; the hard parts were operations, local entities and compliance in several countries, not software.

defensibility.rationale: Recruiting and employer of record services are widely offered; local offices, called Howdy Houses, and community give some stickiness.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Marketplaces and payroll platforms named by Hacker News commenters in 2022 were not shown to copy the Howdy model; Howdy acquired Brazilian GeekHunter in August 2023.

market_need_then: US startups faced an engineering talent shortage and remote work grew in 2020 and 2021; founders said they struggled at OwnLocal to compete for talent and used Latin American outsourcing partners.

branding.name_origin: Started as Austin Software in 2018, renamed Astro, then Howdy in November 2022; the company said it outgrew the old name and chose Howdy, a Texas greeting that reflects friendly, warm and a little weird values (smartbranding.com summary of company statement, seen in search results).
branding.domain_note: Moved to the shorter howdy.com domain with the Nov 2022 rebrand, per press summary; purchase terms not found.
branding.brand_signature: Howdy Houses, physical hubs for engineers in Latin American cities

rebrands.why: Not stated in sources opened; Launch HN at YC W21 used Astro
Outgrew the name and wanted a short memorable friendly name

branding.community_and_virality: Hosts meetups and a community of engineers in Howdy Houses per the company's YC description.

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive, memorable real word name and owned physical community hubs, but a service business with limited independent brand coverage.

outcome_analysis: Howdy, founded in 2018 as Austin Software, joined YC in Winter 2021 as Astro and came out of stealth in August 2022 with a 13 million dollar Series A led by Greycroft, followed by a 5 million dollar extension in January 2023 at a reported 105 million valuation. It bought GeekHunter in August 2023 and reports hundreds of staff and more than 200 client companies. Remote work demand and the founders' own hiring pain drove growth; margins and later funding are not public.
notes: Total raised 15.9 million including the Series A per TechCrunch, implying about 2.9 million earlier that is not itemised, so coverage is partial. Contxto dates the 13 million round November 2022 while TechCrunch and BuiltIn say August 2022; August used. BuiltIn gives 18 million total for the Series A, others say 21 million total raised. Competitors Toptal and Turing come from a Launch HN thread whose exact date was not shown (about mid 2022, over a year after the batch), so treat as later context. The 2021 'USD 5 million' plan in Contxto conflicts with its own dates. YC batch W21.
